purpose: Durably cluster RFC-0002 GitHub issue learnings so future implementation slices inspect related defects, preserve no-claim boundaries, and update context or skills when repeated patterns recur.

patterns.title: GitHub issue state, closure wording, docs, wiki, and agent-context truth must remain executable and mainline-backed.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Before changing RFC-0002 truth, run the execution ledger gate and live state audit, generate the issue execution summary instead of relying on chat or ad hoc assignee filters, and generate the live cross-repo posture from the governed owner/dependency repository set rather than a hand-maintained subset. Preserve Keep-open wording for partial issues, ensure partial PR title/body text uses neutral verbs instead of GitHub auto-close keywords, ensure parent open_tracker issues carry status/tracker, reject conflicting status/* lifecycle labels on ledger-tracked issues, and record exact PR/main/wiki/branch evidence on the owning issue. Live state-audit fetches must query the repository issue total, request that complete result set, and fail when the returned cardinality differs; targeted ledger backfills alone cannot detect a newly RFC-labeled issue outside a fixed list window. Open blocked ledger entries must declare current external issue dependencies through canonical currentBlockerIssueRefs values in owner/repo#number form whenever a specific issue is asserted as a current blocker; the live state audit must fail if a declared blocker is missing or closed, and historical closed references must not remain structured as current blockers. Run the scheduled live posture-snapshot gate after issue-label or lifecycle changes, keep the source snapshot within its explicit age tolerance, and date every current-count prose claim with the same as-of date. Before creating a partial RFC-0002 PR from a saved body, run scripts/github_issue_pr_text_gate.py with --title-file or --title plus --body-file against that exact artifact so local evidence matches the text that will reach GitHub. Treat that PR-text gate as a fail-closed precondition before gh pr create, gh pr edit, or branch-head refresh; PowerShell flows must check $LASTEXITCODE immediately and stop on failure so unsafe keep-open wording cannot be followed by a later GitHub mutation in the same loose command group. Negated issue references such as `does not close #681` are unsafe because GitHub still matches the closing keyword and issue reference; describe non-completion without an issue reference. Governance terms such as fail-closed are safe only when they are not immediately followed by an issue reference; direct phrases such as `closed #681` or `fail closed #681` must still fail closed. Pending final-closure and post-completion issues must carry status/blocked, not status/ready, while prerequisite RFC blockers remain open; their richer pending execution status remains in the ledger and summary. Classify every open status/blocked cross-repo RFC-0002 issue through the blocker classification contract: Core, production identity/session authority, protected runtime/deployment evidence, provider/bank/legal approval, final-closure prerequisites, and certification evidence may remain blocked; writable app-code work must move out of blocked posture and become ready or in-progress. Treat RFC-0002 counts as label-backed execution truth; title-only GitHub references must be reported separately until deliberately labeled and ledgered. Current/live documentation posture must cite counts that match contracts/implementation-proof/rfc0002-issue-posture-snapshot.v1.json; update that contract from the governed summary/posture commands before editing docs, and preserve older counts only in explicitly historical or then-current prose. When a partial merge changes implementation truth, blocker state, support posture, wiki source, context, or policy, update the source-controlled ledger closure instruction and operator docs with the exact PR, main SHA, primary/security runs, wiki decision, and branch cleanup evidence instead of leaving older current-main references behind. When a codebase review ledger entry references a closed merged-main issue, mark the review row closed or hardened on main and cite exact PR, main SHA, mainline validation, issue state, wiki decision, and branch cleanup; documentation-contract gate coverage should prevent stale `Fixed locally` / PR-pending review rows from surviving after closure. When the GitHub issue closure matrix references a closed merged-main issue, mark the row `merged_main`, cite exact PR/main/Main Releasability/CodeQL evidence, and add that issue to the immutable merged-main guard so stale `locally_fixed` rows cannot survive after closure. Closure-sync PRs that deliberately auto-close a source-marked closed issue must avoid exact Keep-open wording for unrelated tracker issues in the PR body, then run the live state audit after merge and label synchronization. Evidence-only Slice 18 synchronization PRs must not recursively require another source-sync PR for their own post-merge evidence; record their final proof as a #681 GitHub issue comment with PR URL, merged main SHA, exact-main Main Releasability run, wiki publication or no-wiki-change decision, and branch/worktree hygiene. If the PR-text gate fails, edit the PR body and create a fresh PR event with a source-controlled push before rerunning because Actions reruns can retain the stale pull_request payload. For #871-style ledger-gate maintainability fixes, keep static issue sets and required evidence fragments in a versioned implementation-proof policy contract, keep Python gates responsible for behavior, and update the execution ledger plus learning-pattern ledger before source mutation so GitHub issue truth remains durable. For #950/#953/#956/#960-style ledger, posture, and proof-artifact test maintainability fixes, keep long evidence-preservation assertions, cross-repo fixture payloads, evidence note signatures, artifact binding tables, and expected posture outputs as named data plus small assertion helpers so future source-sync updates change protected evidence deliberately without creating oversized test functions or weakening ledger/posture/proof-artifact gate behavior. When refactoring implementation-proof readiness API or CLI artifact input wiring, route configured artifacts through typed ImplementationProofReadinessProofInputs group adapters rather than broad legacy keyword fan-out, preserve no-claim authority boundaries, and update the execution ledger before opening a PR.
nonClaimBoundaries: Issue state labels are not proof; they must point to PR, SHA, run, wiki, and branch evidence.
Slice 18 context updates do not complete RFC-0002 while implementation slices remain open.

patterns.title: Workbench and Gateway product-surface proof must be backed by route, panel, action, feedback, conversion-intent, and identity evidence.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Treat local/test caller fixtures and static Workbench or Gateway declarations as non-certifying until owner route proof, UI consumption proof, and production identity evidence are available. Runtime UI consumption must arrive through the Gateway/Workbench runtime-execution proof consumer and may clear only its named BFF-consumption blocker while preserving production identity, accessibility, canonical demo, data-product, client-publication, suitability/execution, and supported-feature blockers. Nested API route modules are inside the caller-context contract gate and must not bypass trusted-caller provenance or strict role-and-capability enforcement. When refactoring review-queue API route composition, keep caller-context construction, role/capability authorization, entitlement-scope intersection, snapshot-token ProblemDetails, operation-event emission, and response projection as named API-boundary responsibilities; do not convert route maintainability into a Workbench/Gateway runtime proof or supported-feature claim. When refactoring candidate-detail API route composition, keep caller-context parsing, role/capability authorization, application command execution, entitlement-scope denial, not-found mapping, durable-storage posture, source-safe response projection, ProblemDetails, and operation-event emission as named API-boundary responsibilities while preserving authorization ordering and non-promotion semantics. When refactoring PostgreSQL review-queue readiness SQL, keep base candidate selection, exclusion classification, duplicate accounting, summary projection, parameter ordering, and every QueueExclusionReason alias as explicit adapter-owned boundaries so Workbench proof consumers keep stable readiness semantics. For source-owned feedback reason codes, canonicalize once at the Idea domain boundary and use the same stable sequence for business-resource identity, persistence, replay, API response, and owner evidence; do not repair an already persisted Idea event in Gateway or Workbench, and preserve raw transport-idempotency conflict semantics when a caller reuses the same key with a changed payload. Apply the same ownership rule to action-owned review-decision reasons: the owner reason appears first and exactly once, caller reasons retain their order, transport-key conflict remains raw-payload based, and downstream surfaces do not rewrite persisted events.
nonClaimBoundaries: Local/test caller authority fixtures are not production identity, authentication, or authorization proof.
Backend source contracts alone do not prove populated Workbench panel readiness.

patterns.title: Business candidate identity must remain stable while evidence, material condition, and transport identity evolve independently.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Derive businessIdentityId only from stable tenant, portfolio, opportunity-family, and governed economic-scope meaning. Keep source content hashes, source routes, transport idempotency keys, reason-code order, and representation-only fields out of business identity while preserving them in evidence lineage. Treat equivalent evidence as an evidence-version refresh, material economic change as a material version, and a resolved condition that later returns as a recurrent reopen with an explicit why-back reason. Reconcile these transitions atomically at the repository boundary, prove concurrent PostgreSQL behavior, and reject caller-supplied duplicate authority at every request and worker-manifest boundary. Direct PostgreSQL fixtures must satisfy the current identity-column and candidate-payload contract; fixtures that need distinct opportunities must vary governed economic scope rather than source hashes. Preserve manual review suppression and snooze as review posture; do not conflate either with evaluator-level duplicate detection. When execution status changes, run the dedicated current-backlog assertion and the full unit lane so durable governance cannot drift from live delivery state. Update migrations, API/OpenAPI, RFC/docs/wiki/context, and the execution ledger together without promoting a supported feature.
nonClaimBoundaries: Stable Idea business identity does not transfer ownership of source financial facts or calculations from Core, Risk, Performance, Advise, or Manage.
Repository reconciliation and local PostgreSQL proof do not certify Gateway/Workbench behavior, production identity/session authority, or supported-feature promotion.

patterns.title: Core, Advise, Manage, Report, Render, and Archive handoffs require owner runtime or materialization evidence before blockers clear.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Classify each downstream artifact by evidence class first: source-contract evidence can support readiness, but only accepted owner runtime receipts or owner materialization records can clear live execution, render, archive, or publication blockers. For conversion-governance API maintenance, keep conversion-intent and conversion-outcome mutation plumbing shared where entitlement, idempotency, durable-write, persistence-problem, and operation-event behavior must remain aligned, while leaving capability, route, response, and non-claim differences explicit. For report evidence-pack API maintenance, keep report-evidence mutation context, application command execution, permission/conflict/invalid-request mapping, persistence-problem projection, operation-event preservation, and response assembly as separately reviewable API-boundary responsibilities while preserving Idea request-recording authority only; do not turn route maintainability into Report, Render, Archive, client-publication, or supported-feature proof. For downstream submission API maintenance, centralize shared caller validation, idempotency validation, durable-write guarding, problem mapping, telemetry emission, and response shaping while keeping conversion-intent versus report-evidence resource identity, source-authority mapping, client lookup, and application command construction route-explicit; do not let API orchestration cleanup imply live owner acceptance or downstream authority. For downstream-realization readiness maintainability, keep the public readiness snapshot behavior stable while splitting orchestration into named helpers for count loading, capability/contract construction, proof application, blocker aggregation, source-of-truth mapping, and final snapshot assembly. Keep readiness DTOs, capability/contract catalog construction, and proof application in bounded modules so later Slice 12/13 work cannot silently mix data shape, static catalog truth, source-contract support, and runtime blocker clearing in one near-cap file. Keep source-contract supporting-evidence proof application separate from runtime-execution blocker-clearing proof application, and test runtime proof consumers against no-route-promotion boundaries when owner route evidence is not certified. Keep registered-proof validation and per-capability mapping centralized in `implementation_proof_consumption.py` so storage, AI, downstream, data-mesh, operator-workflow, and Workbench/Gateway proof families cannot drift on artifact-effect enforcement, current-proof validation, evidence refs, blocker clearing, or supported-feature non-promotion semantics. For downstream outcome certification maintainability, keep owner-runtime proof assembly, proof-check evaluation, and final payload projection separate while preserving #379 as the live downstream certification authority and retaining every non-proof claim boundary. For Advise and Manage intake runtime proof-generator maintenance, keep inline owner-app test-client script construction, environment construction, subprocess execution, JSON-object decoding, and source-safe receipt projection as named reviewable responsibilities while preserving accepted/replay/rejected/idempotency-conflict/authorization-denied/tenant-scoped scenarios. For Manage, bounded action-intake receipts may clear only the live-route blocker and must preserve action-register, rebalance, order, publication, production, and support blockers. Manage mandate runtime proof may consume source-owned temporal receipt identity only when evidence-as-of date, producer-generated time, temporal identity status, source batch fingerprint, and source-ref as-of posture reconcile; it must still preserve production trusted caller-context blockers until an IdP/session/token-claims authority exists. When refactoring the Manage mandate runtime-evidence contract, keep request-scope reconciliation, Manage temporal identity reconciliation, Performance/Risk source qualification, source-ref digest reconstruction, action-register supportability, and allocation-drift outcome validation as named reviewable responsibilities; do not let maintainability work clear #379 or imply downstream/live certification. For bond maturity runtime-evidence qualification, keep Core maturity source-ref authority, Core holdings upstream source-ref authority, entitlement posture, product identity, response tenant/portfolio scope, maturity-window semantics, maturity basis, count validity, maturity fact consistency, supportability status, and source-authority proof as explicit reviewable responsibilities; do not let maintainability work clear Workbench/Gateway, data-mesh, client-publication, supported-feature, production-identity, deployment-certification, or final RFC blockers. For Report materialization, bounded runtime receipts may clear report_evidence_pack_live_materialization_proof_missing, rendered_output_creation_missing, and archive_record_creation_missing only when accepted archived receipts are bound to exact Render and Archive owner-mainline evidence; they must preserve client-publication, production-identity, legal/retention, support, final-certification, and supported-feature blockers.
nonClaimBoundaries: Idea owns opportunity intent and evidence-pack request posture, not suitability approval, rebalance execution, report rendering, archive retention, or client publication.
Quarantined or fixture-backed outcome history is diagnostic and does not certify downstream persistence.

patterns.title: Adviser feedback needs governed product semantics and privacy-safe offline evaluation without automatic policy mutation.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Keep feedback outcome, feedback reason, and review action as distinct canonical facts. Validate allowed outcome/reason combinations at the domain boundary, carry the same taxonomy through mutation identity, persistence, replay, audit, outbox, API/OpenAPI, and Workbench consumption, and reject free-form or UI-invented policy authority. Build only tenant-scoped, source-safe, reproducible offline evaluation projections with explicit policy/version provenance. Never mutate production eligibility, score, rank, suppression, lifecycle, or AI training automatically from feedback.
nonClaimBoundaries: Durable feedback and offline evaluation evidence are not automatic learning or production policy approval.
Workbench consumes the Idea-owned taxonomy and does not own or translate its semantics.

patterns.title: Opportunity quality must be measured through governed funnels, rank quality, timing, and downstream posture rather than raw candidate volume.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Define the effectiveness read model before adding metrics: every rate needs an explicit numerator, denominator, time window, inclusion/exclusion policy, zero-denominator result, current-outcome selection, and correction/reopen rule. Aggregate in the repository with bounded tenant-scoped index-supported queries and independently prove parity against domain fixtures. Separate bounded analytical output from low-cardinality Prometheus metrics; never label metrics with client, portfolio, candidate, actor, correlation, or raw reason identity. Preserve downstream outcome authority and do not interpret uncertain or timeout posture as success.
nonClaimBoundaries: Operational counters and metric availability are not evidence that adviser usefulness improved.
Effectiveness measurement does not grant suitability, recommendation, downstream outcome, or supported-feature authority.

patterns.title: Cross-family opportunity quality needs independently authored golden expectations over production policy paths.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Maintain a versioned, independently authored opportunity-quality golden set that invokes production family policy, scoring, queue, and lifecycle paths. Handwrite expected candidate and abstention outcomes, reason codes, score components, rank, evidence posture, identity refresh, suppression or expiry, and reopen behavior; never generate expectations from the policy under test. Keep source-owned facts as explicit synthetic fixtures, preserve family-specific methodology, and resist a generic signal framework, endpoint, runtime service, production-data capture, or supported-feature claim.
nonClaimBoundaries: A deterministic local evaluation set is product regression evidence, not live source, Gateway, Workbench, downstream, deployment, or production certification.
Synthetic source facts do not grant Idea authority over portfolio, performance, risk, mandate, suitability, or advisory methodology.

patterns.title: Data-product promotion and runtime trust telemetry require mesh catalog, policy, discovery, and supported-feature evidence to agree.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Use the shared supported-feature promotion evaluator and runtime trust telemetry posture instead of independent status counters or static catalog inclusion claims.
nonClaimBoundaries: Mesh policy or catalog source contracts alone do not certify data-product publication.
Runtime trust telemetry snapshots do not promote customer-facing supported features without current evidence and owner approvals.

patterns.title: Operations, security, lifecycle, migration, outbox, SLO, capacity, and disaster-recovery claims need protected or production-like attestations.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Separate contract-green local posture from protected execution evidence; do not clear capacity, lifecycle, migration, broker, DR, vulnerability, or incident-response blockers with static files, local-only probes, or stale report-only evidence. For #343/#344/#375/#797-style operations blockers, record which repository-owned controls are mainline-backed and which protected, bank, provider, environment-secret, target-database, workflow-run, approval, incident-commander, escalation, or post-incident problem-management evidence remains absent before changing status. Treat pyproject build-system roots as governed dependency posture inputs; exact runtime/dev pins are insufficient if build backend/tooling can resolve through unpinned or range-based requirements. For #807-style container findings, first remove final-image package installers, build tools, caches, and vendored metadata that are not application runtime dependencies; do not add scanner exceptions for removable installer-only artifacts, and prove the result with docker build, container image scan, and runtime smoke evidence. Link any future vulnerability exception to the platform-wide exception register with a VX-* platform identity, current platform schema ref, affected version or digest, exposure and exploitability assessments, planned remediation path, and active/no-active register status that matches the exception list; platform report-only validation remains non-certifying before promotion. For #814-style canonical capacity-seed authorization failures, fix the writable app/orchestration contract by calling public APIs with complete synthetic entitlement scope and a bounded local trusted-caller marker; do not weaken endpoint authorization and do not classify writable local authorization wiring as an external blocker. For downstream-capacity seed adapter maintenance, normalize all outbound request timestamps to canonical UTC `Z` at the HTTP boundary and reject naive timestamps before network I/O so replay identity, operation timing, and cross-repo capacity-proof comparison stay deterministic. For service capacity workload CLI maintenance, keep argument/timing validation, downstream seed/path resolution, paced measurement execution, optional evidence loading, attestation verification, platform cost verification, baseline artifact construction, and atomic output as named reviewable boundaries; do not convert the maintainability refactor into #345/#814 capacity certification or supported-feature closure. For outbox delivery maintainability, keep operator-run idempotency and no-mutation replay/conflict handling before event claiming, keep lease context construction explicit, isolate single-event publisher/repository result classification so broker-rejection, dead-letter, already-published, not-found, and lease-lost races remain source-safe and reviewable, and keep PostgreSQL readiness summary SQL, status/time parameter ordering, empty-summary fallback, and aggregate row projection as separately reviewable boundaries so pending, leased, failed, published, dead-letter, due-retry, retry-deferred, expired-lease, and oldest-ready semantics cannot drift. For outbox platform-mesh source-contract proof builder maintenance, keep contract payload loading, source-safety checks, event-family coverage, platform manifest/catalog qualification, evidence-class compatibility, and no-claim payload assembly as named reviewable responsibilities; source-contract evidence must remain unable to clear runtime publication, deployment, Gateway/Workbench, supported-feature, client-publication, or production certification blockers. For Dockerfile runtime release-evidence validator maintenance, keep base-image/runtime metadata, runtime dependency, runtime entrypoint, prohibited-fragment, secret-like build metadata, and dependency-install ordering checks as separately reviewable rule families; do not bury dependency or image-governance policy changes inside a broad validator edit. For main releasability image publication, treat registry secondary-rate-limit errors as transient infrastructure faults only when all prior build/smoke/scan/SBOM steps are healthy; use bounded retry/backoff around GHCR authentication, image publish, and digest resolution while preserving fail-closed release evidence, immutable digest capture, signing, provenance, SBOM, license, and identity validation. For trusted tenant-context gate maintenance, keep access-scope, Core source-port, Core adapter, Core-backed application, source-ingestion identity, signal API support, API base-model, observability, route-level trusted caller-context, and required-test coverage checks as separately reviewable rule families; do not turn contract-gate maintainability into production IdP/session-token implementation or supported-feature promotion. For source-ingestion readiness maintenance, keep readiness path resolution, scheduled-worker source-contract validation, deployment-evidence validation, and configured-path availability as separately reviewable helpers; when a module intentionally re-exports imported constants for tests or callers, preserve explicit self-alias imports so full-repo MyPy `--no-implicit-reexport` gates remain green. For source-ingestion run-once API route maintainability, keep caller-context parsing, operator authorization, durable repository posture, capacity shedding, runtime blocker mapping, runtime execution dispatch, dependency-error mapping, cleanup suppression, and `supportedFeaturePromoted=false` posture as separately reviewable API-boundary responsibilities; do not convert route maintainability into live Core certification, Workbench/Gateway proof, data-mesh promotion, production identity, supported-feature promotion, or runtime topology change. For data-lifecycle API route maintainability, keep trusted caller authorization, lifecycle authority verification, Archive lifecycle posture verification, command construction, durable repository execution, and response/problem projection as separately reviewable API-boundary responsibilities; do not turn a maintainability refactor into legal/privacy certification, Archive production conformance, IdP/session-token implementation, Gateway/Workbench proof, supported-feature promotion, or runtime topology change. For candidate-lifecycle API route maintainability, keep trusted caller construction, lifecycle capability authorization, idempotency validation, durable repository configuration guard, event-lineage/command construction, application execution, response projection, persistence-problem projection, and operation-event preservation as separately reviewable API-boundary responsibilities; do not convert local trusted-caller headers into production IdP/session-token authority or supported-feature promotion. For review feedback API route maintainability, keep feedback mutation context, application command execution, permission and entitlement denial mapping, invalid-request mapping, persistence-problem projection, operation-event preservation, and response assembly as separately reviewable API-boundary responsibilities while preserving event-lineage, idempotency, durable-storage, and `supportedFeaturePromoted=false` semantics. For report evidence-pack API route maintainability, keep report-evidence mutation context, application command execution, permission/conflict/invalid-request mapping, persistence-problem projection, durable-write guard, operation-event preservation, and response assembly as separately reviewable API-boundary responsibilities while preserving Idea-only request recording, Report/Render/Archive non-authority, and `supportedFeaturePromoted=false` semantics. Once the canonical run reaches Idea build/seed and full-stack bring-up, drains valuation and aggregation queues, reports current Core/Gateway dates, and then fails in Core with positions_data_quality_status=UNKNOWN, classify the remaining blocker as Core positions data-quality metadata convergence tracked by sgajbi/lotus-core#836 rather than as an Idea authorization or Workbench orchestration defect. If a later canonical rerun reaches COMPLETE data-quality and current Core/Gateway dates but remains blocked by in-window unleased PENDING portfolio_aggregation_jobs, classify it as a Core aggregation claim/supersession/readiness blocker such as sgajbi/lotus-core#873; do not close Render, Workbench, Idea, or supported-feature proof issues from partial readiness, and do not manually mutate Core tables to manufacture evidence. If the canonical path reaches Manage candidate discovery and fails with BULK_REVIEW_CAMPAIGN_SOURCE_HASH_REQUIRED, first verify live GitHub state for sgajbi/lotus-core#882; when #882 is closed, do not keep #814/#685/#686 classified as Core-blocked and instead require fresh governed PB_SG_GLOBAL_BAL_001 runtime proof across Idea seed, Gateway-backed Workbench queue/detail reads, and browser review-action/feedback/conversion-intent controls. Do not fabricate Core source hashes in Manage, Gateway, Workbench, or Idea, and do not reuse stale runtime artifacts after a Core blocker lands. Keep incident-response customer-communication and production-certification language source-safe until bank-approved communication authority, production identity, and protected operational evidence exist.
nonClaimBoundaries: Local/disposable database drills are not provider backup, PITR, failover, or production certification.
Static SLO, dashboard, lifecycle, outbox, incident-response, or dependency posture contracts are non-certifying until runtime/protected/release evidence exists.

patterns.title: AI explanation output acceptance requires attested lotus-ai execution, model provenance, retention, and lineage evidence.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Keep deterministic fallback/local AI output and static workflow-pack registration separate from live provider attestation; only signed, source-safe, retention-bound runtime execution can clear #340. When an AI runtime proof cites an actual runtime receipt, validate temporal provenance coherently: the proof artifact cannot be generated before the runtime receipt it cites, and aggregate readiness should preserve the runtime blocker or emit a source-safe provenance diagnostic instead of accepting internally inconsistent evidence. For signed AI attestation and workflow-pack registration source-contract maintainability refactors, keep source-authority assembly, producer contract checks, consumer contract checks, proof-check construction, evidence-class evaluation, unsupported-claim flags, validity derivation, and payload projection separately reviewable; preserve closed payload fields and prove source-contract evidence does not set runtime, provider, deployment, model-risk, Workbench, client-publication, supported-feature, or certification flags. For #1065-style AI workflow output unsafe-shape API contract proof refactors, keep the public test behavior stable while separating valid request setup, invalid claim/action/output payload variants, duplicate claim identity checks, timezone validation, and validation-error assertions; do not convert DTO validation cleanup into production provider, model-risk, API/OpenAPI, supported-feature, or final-RFC certification claims. For #1101-style AI workflow output evaluator refactors, keep action-policy evaluation and canonical action-label projection, action blocker projection, unsupported source-product claim detection, grounded accepted-result construction, provider-output integrity digest chaining, audit-event projection, and non-authority posture as separately reviewable boundaries while preserving public evaluator behavior and avoiding production provider/model-risk, Gateway/Workbench, supported-feature, or final-RFC claims.
nonClaimBoundaries: Idea does not implement lotus-ai provider execution, model approval, or provider retention authority.
Local fallback output is diagnostic and cannot certify workflow output acceptance.

patterns.title: Demo readiness, commercial proof, canonical archetypes, and full live journey claims must be implementation-backed end to end.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Treat commercial language as downstream of evidence: canonical opportunity archetypes, demo claim matrices, and live journeys must cite current implementation proof and preserve blockers where source-owner runtime evidence is absent. Treat missing work inside writable Lotus app/platform repositories as fix-forward scope, not blocked; reserve blocked posture for external or non-writable dependencies such as core-owner work that must be issue-backed. Keep archetype domain-policy implementations modular: separate guard/decision flow from identity, signal, lineage, evidence-packet, and candidate construction, and add focused identity-alignment tests before claiming a policy refactor preserves behavior. For canonical opportunity-archetype evidence-pack builder maintenance, keep timestamp/scope validation, canonical archetype projection, blocker aggregation, source-authority boundary, canonical portfolio scope, claim boundary, source-of-truth projection, pack summary, evidence refs, and final payload digest assembly separately reviewable; preserve canonical portfolio hash-only handling and never turn source-contract evidence into Gateway, Workbench, client-publication, data-mesh, supported-feature, production identity, or demo-certification proof. For opportunity-archetype implementation-proof application maintenance, keep proof application scope-driven through named proof-step descriptors instead of broad keyword fan-out; prove valid blocker-clearing and invalid/missing proof fail-closed behavior through focused tests while preserving registered artifact-effect enforcement and no-claim boundaries. For opportunity proof-step catalog maintenance, group proof-step construction by evidence-source family while preserving payload argument names, ref argument names, validator and applicator bindings, deterministic ordering, blocker-clearing effect enforcement, freshness checks, source-safe fail-closed behavior, supported-feature non-promotion, and no-claim boundaries. For low-income cashflow-pressure evaluation, preserve Core-owned cashflow and cash-movement source authority, access-scope identity binding, and review-candidate-only posture when extracting helpers or modules.
nonClaimBoundaries: Research, blueprint language, and demo copy cannot promote unsupported features.
A single capability proof does not certify the full API, Gateway, Workbench, and downstream handoff journey.

patterns.title: Quality-baseline hotspots need issue-backed decomposition without changing product claims.
patterns.futureAgentRule: When `make quality-baseline` surfaces a large helper in RFC-0002 proof tests, documentation-governance gates, platform runtime composition, API-boundary orchestration, deterministic domain signal evaluation, hash-bound production domain assembly, production PostgreSQL readiness projections, or CI/proof contract gates, duplicate-check GitHub first, create or reuse one focused issue, preserve behavior through focused tests, and split by domain, route, contract-envelope, consumer, or rule-family responsibility rather than by arbitrary line count. Keep production, schema, migration, supported-feature, Core, Gateway, Workbench, and final-RFC claims explicitly out of scope unless those surfaces actually changed; if route metadata is touched, run OpenAPI gates and state clearly whether public API contracts changed; if canonical hashes or persisted payloads are touched, prove exact content-integrity behavior and tamper rejection before claiming maintainability closure. For #1006-style execution-summary test refactors, keep count derivation, status-bucket rendering, slice membership, learning-pattern current issue rendering, and negative stale-issue assertions explicit through named helpers so source-truth count updates do not require weakening behavior checks. For #1010-style implementation-proof documentation gate refactors, keep duplicate-key, CLI-drift, readiness-argument, and inventory evidence-classification checks as named fail-closed validators under the same public entry point. For #1027-style implementation-proof readiness API posture tests, split envelope, blocker, capability-catalog, proof-family, supported-feature non-promotion, and source-safe redaction assertions into named helpers while preserving every blocked-posture assertion. For #1029-style configured proof-artifact readiness API tests, split configured artifact blocker clearing, residual blocker preservation, evidence-ref consumption, per-proof-family posture, and source-safe redaction assertions into named helpers without changing runtime proof semantics or supported-feature posture. For #1033-style platform route-registration refactors, split route metadata into route-owned helpers while preserving paths, handlers, response models, tags, summaries, descriptions, examples, and health/version behavior. For #1037-style runtime evidence validator refactors, split payload-envelope, no-claim boundary, receipt integrity, execution-success, and control-list checks into named helpers while preserving the public validator signature, return semantics, source authority, blocker/evidence refs, and supported-feature non-promotion. For #1040-style configured implementation-proof artifact loader changes, keep runtime binding definitions typed and make unit coverage assert exact parity with JSON and ref-only loader bindings so future proof inputs cannot be added without matching source-safe ref/provenance tests. For #1044-style behavioral repository refactors, keep idempotency, resource lookup, progression-policy validation, accepted-record mutation, index updates, audit, and outbox payload construction as named boundaries while preserving repository port signatures and no-claim posture. For #1047/#1049-style PostgreSQL proof-test refactors, keep lease/retry/publish/reload and lifecycle preview/replay/hold/erasure/retention/purge/telemetry phases as named proof steps while preserving DB-backed behavior and requiring PR/main PostgreSQL Runtime Proof before closure. For #1052-style report evidence-pack integration proof refactors, preserve the public endpoint-certification test hook while splitting conversion-intent setup, replay/conflict, client-publication guardrail, authority/resource failure, invalid request-shape, and assertion responsibilities into named helpers; do not convert Idea request recording into Report/Render/Archive materialization, client publication, supported-feature, Gateway/Workbench, or final-RFC proof.
